N966-quantum-channel-conditional-sld-order | Conditional Umegaki order for quantum channels is equivalent to complete equal-reference SLD order
status=source_derived_unreviewed; source internal audits are accepted only at exact version and scope through a knowledge review overlay. External correctness/priority, physical evidence and practical advantage remain separately scoped.

EXACT CLAIM
For arbitrary finite-dimensional quantum channels P,Q with the same input, the uniform conditional Umegaki relative-entropy order with constant c is equivalent to the complete equal-reference SLD metric order with the same c. Taking Q to be identity identifies the conditional Umegaki contraction coefficient with the complete equal-reference SLD coefficient.

SOURCE-REPORTED INTERFACE
Finite-dimensional channels, arbitrary finite references, faithful states and faithful baselines; output supports are restricted to effective support and finite boundary cases use common faithful regularization.

BOUNDARIES
No equality with complete equal-reference Umegaki for arbitrary quantum channels follows. The N675 source contributes only its selected Section 2 saturated-reference filter; hardness and compiler claims remain unreviewed.

PRIOR ART AND TRANSFER LIMIT
The coherent-qubit SLD-to-BKM integral is prior work by Hirche, in Quantum estimation, channel orders, and private capacity, arXiv:2610.03706v1, Proposition 3.5 / Eq. (3.18). The conditional reference-score gauge, saturated-reference reverse filter, and state-pair interpolation in this result are distinct receiving steps. The integral alone supplies no general positive equal-reference Umegaki witness.

COST AND INFORMATION BOUNDARY
Finite-dimensional operator and relative-entropy calculations; no physical implementation is claimed.

NEXT OBLIGATION
External priority and any extension beyond the stated finite-dimensional contract remain open.

evidence.quote: Read governing proofs: Proposition 3.5 / Eq. (3.18); Theorem 3.2 / Appendix A.1; Section 2.2 / Eq. (2.12); Proposition 3.4 / Appendix A.2; Theorem 5.1. The coherent-qubit integral must be credited as prior. The smoothed criterion has a finite reference test dimension d_B²; this is not an unsmoothed-reference cutoff. Section 6 leaves the unsmoothed-to-signed-lift implication open generally.
evidence.status: Exact selected source bytes; internal acceptance applies only through a version-bound overlay.

evidence.quote: The conditional gauge remains a separate step in our argument. For arbitrary input baseline σ and tangent H, let L=Omega_(σ_R)^−1(H_R) and H0=H−Omega_σ(I tensor L). Then H0_R=0, and the output conditional SLD deficit equals the full SLD norm of the channel image of H0. The channel commutes with this reference-only gauge. Applying the prior integral pointwise and integrating BKM along a segment proves our quantitative conditional sufficiency for every coefficient c≥0.
evidence.status: Exact selected source bytes; internal acceptance applies only through a version-bound overlay.

evidence.quote: Our reverse construction in `universal_conditional_sld_equivalence.md` is different: it uses a saturated numerator reference and finite resolvent filters converging to a point kernel. Its pair has unequal reference marginals. Nothing in the coherent-qubit integral alone supplies that reverse realization. Conversely, neither argument produces a physical equal-reference Umegaki witness for a general quantum channel from an arbitrary conditional witness. That remains the previously isolated positivity problem.
